audit_sample.blinding: the auditor receives only fn_audit_sheet.csv: audit id, title and DOI, rows in one stable shuffle (sha256('sela-fn-audit-2026-10-26|blinded-order|<source>:<candidate_id>')) across all strata, so neither the stratum nor the machine priority can be inferred from the order; fn_audit_key.csv (stratum, machine priority, v3 priority if eligible, eligibility basis) is joined on audit_id only after the audit
audit_sample.criterion: doc 14 acceptance criterion 5 (manual false-positive / false-negative audit), plus a check of the publication-type eligibility rule

machine_pre_audit_pool_deferred.note: a machine re-screen with lexicon sela-v3-families-2, NOT the manual audit; the auditor columns are blank

audit_sample.selection: first n rows by sha256('sela-fn-audit-2026-10-26|<source>:<stratum>|<candidate_id>'); stable across Python versions; plus deferred pool titles named in the research audit (purposive)

changes_from_previous_screening: lexicon sela-v3-families-2: Indonesian age terms (remaja, anak, siswa, pelajar, lansia, lanjut usia, dewasa) as population signals; Indonesian feature and consent terms (menulis ekspresif, jurnal harian, privasi, kerahasiaan, persetujuan orang tua, bunuh diri, mencari bantuan, disabilitas, ...); a working_age_adults family; every families-1 entry unchanged
Indonesian age phrases ('berusia 15-17 tahun', 'usia 60 tahun ke atas') are read as ages

population band v2: includes_15_17_explicit only when the ages agree on one range or minimum that overlaps 15-17 and the record is not a review; ages that describe an advisory or working group do not count

the false-negative audit is blinded (fn_audit_sheet.csv shows only audit id, title and DOI; fn_audit_key.csv holds the machine labels and is joined after the audit) and adds an excluded_publication_type stratum to check the eligibility rule

indonesian_age_term_titles.note: titles containing remaja, anak, siswa, pelajar, lansia or lanjut usia; a check that Indonesian age words now give a population signal

limitations: Lexical families miss paraphrases and over-match generic words (for example 'trust', 'stress', 'anak'); every label is a prompt for a human screener, not a relevance or quality judgement.
Population bands come from words, MeSH groups and explicit ages in titles/abstracts; adult and adolescent signals are kept apart and are unverified.
possible_null_or_negative_finding is a cue list for finding counter-evidence, not a result.
The worksheet supports dual screening (two reviewers, disagreement resolution); all decisions are blank.
Blinding is procedural: the key file sits next to the sheet and must not be given to the auditor.
population_band_rule: Screening v1.1: includes_15_17_explicit only when the title/abstract ages agree on ONE range or minimum that overlaps 15-17 and the record is not a review (a review's ages are eligibility rules, not one sample), the same rule as the corpus age band; ages that describe an advisory or working group do not count. Any other minor age, or youth words without such a range, is adolescent_or_youth_unverified.
queue_rule: per feature family up to 30 (title hit for that family first, then high before medium, score desc), then the remaining best rows up to 400
screening_unit: title + abstract (abstract read from the local cache only; never committed)

supersedes.note: screening v1.0 of run v1.0 stays frozen and reproducible; v1.1 only adds entries
